mcqs.why: The correct answer is soup in a dish, because the fox invited the stork for dinner and served him soup in a dish.

mcqs.q: What did the stork serve, and in what?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fish in a narrow vase, because the stork invited the fox the next week and served fish in a narrow vase.

mcqs.q: Why could the stork not eat the soup?
options: His long beak could not manage soup thinly spread in the dish
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his long beak could not manage the thinly spread soup, because the text gives this reason and the stork returned home hungry.

mcqs.q: What rule did the stork follow when he served the fox?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is tit for tat, because the text says he did to the fox what the fox had done to him, and Exercise 3 gives tit for tat.

mcqs.q: Which choices did the stork have according to the author?
options: Serve all animals only in jugs, and serve in a broad-base bottle
Only serve in a narrow vase again
Serve in a container suitable for the fox, and invite other animals too and serve each in suitable containers
mcqs.why: The correct answer is options b and c only, because the builder answer confirms only serving suitably and inviting others with suitable containers are correct.

mcqs.q: What does God tell us to do, according to the story message?
options: Replace the bad with the good
mcqs.why: The correct answer is replace the bad with the good, because the listening text states this as the rule we must follow instead of tit for tat.

mcqs.q: What is the listening procedure in Exercise 1?
options: Ask questions while the story is read
Read the questions first, listen when the teacher reads, and do not ask questions while the story is being read
Read the story aloud yourself first
Only draw spider webs without listening
mcqs.why: The correct answer is read questions first and listen without asking questions during reading, because the book instruction states students are not allowed to ask questions when the story is being read.

lessons.title: Fun: Role Play of a Poem
lessons.notes_html:
About the Role Play

This Fun section is for having fun with language and is not to be formally assessed. Students work in trios to plan a role play for the poem A Mountain and a Squirrel by Allama Iqbal. One student should read the poem, one should act as the mountain, and the third one should act as the squirrel. Each trio will present their role play in front of the class. First, students discuss the meanings of the given words, then check their meanings from the glossary. The poem is a translation of Allama Iqbal poem Pahar Aur Gilareeh.

Vocabulary

WordMeaning
self-respectrespect for oneself, dignity
insignificantunimportant, of little value
arrogantproud, thinking oneself better than others
shrewdclever, sharp in judgement
splendourgreat beauty and brightness
poseto pretend to be something one is not
grandeurgreatness, magnificence
expelto drive out
beetlenutthe nut of the betel palm, areca nut
Omnipotenceall-powerfulness of God

What Happens in the Poem

The mountain speaks proudly to the squirrel, calling it insignificant and arrogant, neither wise nor intelligent nor shrewd, and says it is no match in comparison with the mountain splendour and grandeur. The squirrel replies boldly: hold your tongue, expel these immature thoughts from your heart. It does not care that it is not large like the mountain. Everything shows the Omnipotence of God; some large, some small, is the wisdom of God. God created the mountain large, and taught the squirrel climbing large trees. The mountain is unable to walk a single step, while the squirrel can break a beetlenut. The poem ends: Nothing is useless in this world; nothing is bad in God creation.

Remember

  • Work in groups of three: reader, mountain and squirrel.
  • Underline the given words in the poem and check meanings in the glossary.
  • Size is not the only greatness; every creature has its own skill given by God.

mcqs.q: How do students perform the role play of A Mountain and a Squirrel?
options: In trios: one reads the poem, one acts as the mountain, one acts as the squirrel
In groups of ten as a press conference
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in trios with reader, mountain and squirrel, because the book instructs students to work in trios with exactly these three roles.

mcqs.q: Who wrote A Mountain and a Squirrel, and what is its original title given in the book?
options: Allama Iqbal; Lab pay ati hai dua
An unknown poet; The Fox and the Stork
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Allama Iqbal and Pahar Aur Gilareeh, because page 101 labels the poem as a translation of Iqbal poem with that title.

mcqs.q: What does self-respect mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is respect for oneself, dignity, because self-respect is defined with that meaning in the poem vocabulary.

mcqs.q: What does insignificant mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is unimportant, of little value, because the mountain calls the squirrel insignificant with this meaning in the vocabulary list.

mcqs.q: What do arrogant and shrewd mean?
options: Arrogant: proud, thinking oneself better than others; shrewd: clever, sharp in judgement
mcqs.why: The correct answer pairs arrogant with proud superiority and shrewd with clever sharp judgement, exactly as defined for this poem.

mcqs.q: What do splendour and grandeur mean?
options: Splendour: a night insect; grandeur: a nut
Splendour: great beauty and brightness; grandeur: greatness, magnificence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is splendour as great beauty and brightness and grandeur as greatness, because the mountain boasts of both in the poem.

mcqs.q: What do expel and Omnipotence mean?
options: Expel: to drive out; Omnipotence: all-powerfulness of God
mcqs.why: The correct answer is expel means to drive out and Omnipotence means all-powerfulness of God, as the squirrel says to expel immature thoughts and everything shows God Omnipotence.

mcqs.q: What does the mountain claim about the squirrel?
options: It is wiser than the mountain
It is no match in comparison with the mountain splendour
mcqs.why: The correct answer is it is no match compared with the mountain splendour, because the mountain says this proudly in its speech to the squirrel.

mcqs.q: What skill does the squirrel say God taught it, which the mountain cannot do?
options: Climbing large trees, while the mountain is unable to walk a single step
mcqs.why: The correct answer is climbing large trees, because the squirrel says God taught it climbing large trees and the mountain cannot walk a single step.

mcqs.q: What is the final message of the poem?
options: Nothing is useless in this world; nothing is bad in God creation
mcqs.why: The correct answer is nothing is useless and nothing is bad in God creation, because these are the closing lines of the poem on page 101.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Health Problems Caused by Mosquitoes
lessons.notes_html:
Summary

The reading text, Health Problems Caused by Mosquitoes, is about the diseases caused by mosquitoes. The three diseases discussed are malaria, dengue and chikungunya. Their symptoms are so similar that it can be quite difficult to identify them for sure without laboratory testing, but it is important to find out what the exact disease is so that it can be treated properly.

Key Points: The Three Diseases

DiseaseSource of TransmissionOrgans / Cells AttackedMain Symptoms
MalariaInfected mosquitoes; the plasmodium parasite enters through the mosquito's salivaRed blood cells; liver; brain in cerebral malariaHigh fever up to 40 degrees C, chills, sweating, constipation, kidney dysfunction, disorientation
DengueInfected mosquitoes (dengue virus); also infected blood transfusion, organ donation, and mother to childWhite blood cells, antibodies, immune system, capillariesHigh fever, severe body pain, pain behind the eyes, decreased urine output, respiratory difficulties, intense headache, skin rashes, excessive bleeding
ChikungunyaMosquitoes living and breeding near stagnant or polluted waterMuscle cells, joints, skin, connective tissues, central nervous systemFever, skin rash, headache, nausea, vomiting, muscle weakness, severe joint pain, partial loss of taste

Important Facts

  • In cerebral malaria the brain becomes highly infected because the flow of blood to the brain stops.
  • In dengue the virus attacks the white blood cells and other antibodies, so the cells burst and die; this causes fluid leakage, low protein, fluid in the lungs and stomach area, low blood pressure and shock.
  • A person can get chikungunya only once, because after recovering from it, one is immune to it for the rest of one's life.
  • Dengue and chikungunya have similar symptoms: fever, skin rashes and joint pain. The joint pain of chikungunya is more pronounced than that of dengue.
  • In malaria, fever and chills come every two days.
  • These diseases affect our health and the quality of our work, because it takes some time to recover from the weakness caused by them.

Vocabulary

WordMeaning
parasitean organism that lives on or in another organism
transmittedpassed from one person or thing to another
salivathe liquid in the mouth
clota thick lump of blood
chillsshivering cold
constipationdifficulty in passing stool
dysfunctionnot working properly
disorientationconfusion
transfusiongiving blood to a patient
antibodiessubstances in the body that fight germs
immuneprotected against a disease
respiratoryto do with breathing
stagnantnot flowing
contagiousspreading by contact
nauseafeeling like vomiting
fatalcausing death
displayshow
inflammationswelling and redness
intensevery strong
pronouncedclear, strong

Prevention and Advice

  • Wear clothes that keep us fully covered and use net coverings.
  • Live in hygienic surroundings and ensure there is no stagnant water.
  • Apply good quality mosquito repellent and take extra precaution from dawn to dusk.
  • Seek medical help as soon as possible; the earlier these diseases are treated, the quicker the recovery.

Remember: an awareness flow chart for malaria follows the order: Malaria, Cause(s), Symptoms, Prevention, Advice.

mcqs.q: What is the reading text mainly about?
options: The life cycle of a mosquito
Use of pesticides for mosquito control
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Diseases caused by mosquitoes' because the whole text discusses malaria, dengue and chikungunya and their causes, symptoms and prevention.

mcqs.q: Which group shows only the diseases mentioned in the text?
options: Malaria, chikungunya, dengue and cerebral malaria
mcqs.why: The correct answer is malaria, chikungunya, dengue and cerebral malaria, because these are the diseases circled from the text; the other diseases in the list are not mentioned.

mcqs.q: Why is it important to find out what the exact disease is?
options: So that the patient can rest
So that we can tell everyone about it
So that the patient can decide what to do
So that it can be treated properly
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'so that it can be treated properly' because the text says the exact disease must be identified for it to be properly treated.

mcqs.q: Which cells does the malaria parasite attack?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is red blood cells because malaria is caused by plasmodium, which infects the red blood cells after entering through the mosquito's saliva.

mcqs.q: Once the dengue virus enters the system, which system does it affect?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the immune system because the dengue virus attacks the white blood cells and other antibodies, which are part of the immune system.

mcqs.q: In severe cases of dengue, bleeding may occur in the:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the gums and nose because the text's question on severe dengue gives bleeding in the gums and nose as the correct option.

mcqs.q: Chikungunya patients usually have fever with:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is rashes because chikungunya patients usually have fever with rashes, along with headache, nausea and severe joint pain.

mcqs.q: What are the most common diseases caused by mosquito bites?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is malaria, dengue and chikungunya because these are the three diseases the whole reading text is built around.

mcqs.q: Which part of the body becomes highly infected in cerebral malaria?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the brain because in cerebral malaria the stoppage of blood flow to the brain makes the brain highly infected.

mcqs.q: How often does one have fever and chills when one has malaria?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is every two days because the lesson states that in malaria the fever and chills return every two days.

mcqs.q: How often can one get infected with chikungunya, and why?
options: Many times, because it is contagious
Every year, because mosquitoes breed yearly
Only once, because after recovering one is immune to it for life
mcqs.why: The correct answer is only once, because after recovering from chikungunya a person is immune to it for the rest of his or her life.

mcqs.q: Which two of the three diseases have similar symptoms?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is dengue and chikungunya because both of them share the symptoms of fever, skin rashes and joint pain.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'stagnant' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'not flowing' because stagnant water is still water that does not flow, and chikungunya mosquitoes breed near such water.

mcqs.q: What does the word 'parasite' mean?
options: An organism that lives on or in another organism
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'an organism that lives on or in another organism' because plasmodium, the cause of malaria, is described in the lesson as such a parasite.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a correct protection step against these diseases?
options: Keeping stagnant water near the house
Going out carelessly from dawn to dusk
Ensuring there is no stagnant water around us
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ensuring there is no stagnant water because the lesson lists this, along with full-covering clothes, nets and repellent, as a way to protect ourselves.

lessons.title: Listening and Speaking: Expressing Satisfaction and Dissatisfaction Politely
lessons.notes_html:
About the Skill

In this section students learn to express satisfaction and dissatisfaction, fully and partially, politely. The work is done in pairs: one student takes the role of Shama and the other that of Ahmer, the dialogue is practised orally two to three times, the roles are switched, and one more dialogue is added by the students themselves.

Useful Expressions

Expressing SatisfactionExpressing Dissatisfaction
I'm / I was extremely happy with ...I'm not / I wasn't happy with ...
I really enjoyed ...I am / was very disappointed with ...
I loved the way in which ...I don't / didn't like the way ...
I am / was very satisfied with ...I am / was very dissatisfied with ...

The Shama and Ahmer Dialogue

Ahmer asks Shama if she is satisfied with the way the teacher explained the poem. Shama honestly says she did not really understand the explanation and still has a number of things to ask. Ahmer is dissatisfied and does not think the teacher was prepared, but he agrees that yesterday the teacher explained the vocabulary very well. In the completed dialogue, Ahmer hopes the teacher will explain the poem again tomorrow, and Shama says she was very satisfied with yesterday's vocabulary class and really enjoyed the activity.

Key Points from the Practice Contexts

  • Train journey: Sharif is very satisfied with the comfortable seats, but Rayan is very dissatisfied with the air conditioning, which is not working at all; they decide to tell the caretaker politely.
  • Power supply: the spokesman is generally very satisfied because complaints are usually solved in time, but very disappointed with the present breakdown, which has not been solved for 48 hours despite repeated complaints.
  • Teacher to Khalid: the teacher is extremely happy with Khalid's work generally, because he usually does very well in tests, but dissatisfied with his performance in the last couple of tests; Khalid apologises and promises to work harder.

Remember

Satisfaction and dissatisfaction can be partial: a speaker can be happy with one part of a thing and unhappy with another part at the same time, and both feelings should be expressed politely.

mcqs.q: Which expression shows satisfaction?
options: I am very dissatisfied with the service.
I don't like the way he explained it.
I was very disappointed with the result.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I really enjoyed the activity' because the book lists 'I really enjoyed ...' among the expressions for expressing satisfaction.

mcqs.q: Which expression shows dissatisfaction?
options: I loved the way in which she taught.
I am very satisfied with my marks.
I am very dissatisfied with the school bus.
I was extremely happy with the class.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'I am very dissatisfied with the school bus' because 'I am / was very dissatisfied with ...' is one of the book's expressions of dissatisfaction.

mcqs.q: In the dialogue, what is Ahmer dissatisfied with?
options: The way the teacher explained the poem
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the way the teacher explained the poem because Ahmer says he is dissatisfied and does not think the teacher was prepared for that lesson.

mcqs.q: With what was Shama very satisfied?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is yesterday's vocabulary class because Shama says, 'I am very satisfied with yesterday's vocabulary class. I really enjoyed the activity.'

mcqs.q: What does Ahmer hope about the poem lesson?
options: That the class will be cancelled
That the teacher will explain it again tomorrow
That a new teacher will come
That the poem will be changed
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the teacher will explain it again tomorrow because Ahmer says, 'I hope he will explain it again tomorrow.'

mcqs.q: On the train to Multan, with what were Sharif and Rayan dissatisfied?
options: The air conditioning, which was not working
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the air conditioning because Rayan says he is very dissatisfied with the air conditioning as it is not working at all, while the seats are comfortable.

mcqs.q: In the power supply context, why is the spokesman disappointed?
options: The power supply is always bad
The present breakdown has not been solved for 48 hours despite repeated complaints
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the 48-hour breakdown because the spokesman is generally satisfied, but disappointed that this breakdown is unsolved after 48 hours despite repeated complaints.

mcqs.q: What does the teacher tell Khalid?
options: He is extremely happy with his work generally, but dissatisfied with his last couple of tests
He is dissatisfied with all of Khalid's work
Khalid has failed every test this year
Khalid should stop coming to class
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the mixed message because the teacher says he is extremely happy with Khalid generally, but dissatisfied with his performance in the last couple of tests.

mcqs.q: Which pair correctly matches the book's expression boxes?
options: Satisfaction: 'I wasn't happy with ...' ; Dissatisfaction: 'I really enjoyed ...'
Satisfaction: 'I loved the way in which ...' ; Dissatisfaction: 'I don't like the way ...'
Satisfaction: 'I am very dissatisfied with ...' ; Dissatisfaction: 'I am very satisfied with ...'
Satisfaction: 'I was very disappointed with ...' ; Dissatisfaction: 'I was extremely happy with ...'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the second pair because the book puts 'I loved the way in which ...' under satisfaction and 'I don't / didn't like the way ...' under dissatisfaction.

mcqs.q: How is the Shama-Ahmer dialogue to be practised in class?
options: Read silently once and written in notebooks
Memorised word by word for a test
Practised orally in pairs two to three times, then roles are switched
mcqs.why: The correct answer is oral pair practice with switched roles because the book instructs students to practise the dialogue orally, not read it, and to switch roles and practise again.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Simple and Compound Sentences
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

In English, we use three main types of sentences: simple, compound and complex. A use of a variety of sentences makes the writing more interesting. This unit discusses two of them.

  • A Simple Sentence has one subject and one predicate. Example: My mother is a good cook.
  • In a Compound Sentence, two complete sentences are joined together by a comma + conjunction: and, but, for, because, or, nor, etc.

Key Points: Classifying the Book's Sentences

SentenceType
This year has started on a positive note for the students.Simple
The classrooms smell of fresh paint, as they were painted during the holidays.Compound
The students love the newly painted classrooms, and they like the newly polished desks.Compound
Most of the students come to school regularly now.Simple
They actively participate in various class activities.Simple
They are happy with the new look of the school, but they are not happy with the sports facilities that they have.Compound
They have requested their principal for better sports and game facilities.Simple

Joining Sentences: Worked Examples

  • Najma and Rehana studied very hard, so they both got A grades in their exams.
  • Our car is very old, but its engine is in good condition.
  • My brother is a good artist, but he cannot sing at all.
  • The baby cannot walk, but the baby can crawl very fast.
  • You may buy only a new dress now, or you may buy a new dress and new shoes next month.
  • I love gardening, for I can grow my own fresh vegetables.
  • This book is very informative, and it is also very interesting.

Remember

To make writing interesting, first write simple sentences about a topic, then join suitable pairs of them into compound sentences, as is done with the classroom sentences and with Sabiha's letter to Munira, which is rewritten in a mix of simple and compound sentences.

mcqs.q: A simple sentence has:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one subject and one predicate because the book defines a simple sentence in exactly these words, as in 'My mother is a good cook.'

mcqs.q: In a compound sentence, two complete sentences are joined by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a comma plus a conjunction because the book states that two complete sentences are joined together by a comma + conjunction such as and, but, for, because, or, nor.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a simple sentence?
options: The students love the classrooms, and they like the desks.
Their motivation has increased and their enthusiasm is visible.
The students enjoy being outdoors, because they like sports.
Most of the students come to school regularly now.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Most of the students come to school regularly now' because it has one subject and one predicate, while the others join two complete sentences.

mcqs.q: 'The classrooms smell of fresh paint, as they were painted during the holidays.' This sentence is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is compound because, according to the book's exercise key, this sentence joins two complete parts with a conjunction and is marked compound.

mcqs.q: Which conjunction best joins: 'Our car is very old. Its engine is in good condition.'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'but' because the two ideas contrast with each other, and the book joins them as 'Our car is very old, but its engine is in good condition.'

mcqs.q: Join correctly: 'Najma and Rehana studied very hard. They both got A grades in their exams.'
options: Najma and Rehana studied very hard, but they both got A grades in their exams.
Najma and Rehana studied very hard, or they both got A grades in their exams.
Najma and Rehana studied very hard, so they both got A grades in their exams.
Najma and Rehana studied very hard, nor they both got A grades in their exams.
mcqs.why: The correct answer uses 'so' because getting A grades is the result of studying hard, and the book's answer joins the pair with 'so'.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is compound?
options: They have requested their principal for better sports facilities.
They actively participate in various class activities.
This year has started on a positive note for the students.
The flowers in this pot are very colourful, and the flowers in your garden have a lovely fragrance.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the flowers sentence because it joins two complete sentences with a comma and the conjunction 'and'; the other three are simple sentences.

mcqs.q: Which conjunction shows a choice in 'You may buy only a new dress now, ___ you may buy a new dress and new shoes next month'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'or' because the sentence offers a choice between two possibilities, and the book joins this pair with 'or'.

mcqs.q: Why does the book ask students to use a variety of sentences?
options: To make the sentences longer only
To make the writing more interesting
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to make the writing more interesting because the book says the use of a variety of sentences makes the writing more interesting, as in the rewriting of Sabiha's letter.

mcqs.q: Join correctly: 'The baby cannot walk. The baby can crawl very fast.'
options: The baby cannot walk, so the baby can crawl very fast.
The baby cannot walk, or the baby can crawl very fast.
The baby cannot walk, but the baby can crawl very fast.
The baby cannot walk, for the baby can crawl very fast.
mcqs.why: The correct answer uses 'but' because the two ideas are in contrast, and the book's answer is 'The baby cannot walk, but the baby can crawl very fast.'

lessons.title: Language Practice: Narration
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules: Changing Narration

This section revises changing the narration of statements, exclamations, wishes, promises and hopes from direct speech to indirect speech.

Tense Rules for Changing from Direct to Indirect

Direct SpeechIndirect Speech
Present simple / present continuous / present perfect / present perfect continuousPast simple / past continuous / past perfect / past perfect continuous
Past simple / past continuous / past perfectPast perfect / past perfect continuous / past perfect
Past perfect continuousPast perfect continuous (no change)

Reporting Verbs

Direct SpeechIndirect Speech
said + exclamation markexclaimed
said + wishwished
said + hopehoped
said + promisepromised

Key Points: Other Changes Shown in the Examples

  • tomorrow becomes the next day: Abid said that he had many friends and that he had to invite all of them the next day.
  • this year becomes that year: Reshma hoped that she would get admission in the medical college that year.
  • today becomes that day: The student promised that he would do his homework regularly from that day.
  • this becomes that and here becomes there: The blind boy wished that he could see that interesting match on the television; the coach exclaimed that their team had won the champion's trophy there for the first time.
  • will changes to would in the reported clause, as in the children's promise that the next week they would clean the whole house.

Remember

In the story Avoiding Criticism, the same rules are applied to every spoken line: bystanders' comments become reported statements with 'said that', strong feelings become 'exclaimed', and Nasrudin's own thoughts become 'hoped' and 'wished'.

mcqs.q: In indirect speech, the present simple tense of direct speech changes into:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is past simple because the book's tense table shows present tenses moving one step back into the corresponding past tenses in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: What happens to the past perfect continuous tense when speech is changed to indirect?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it remains past perfect continuous because the book's table shows past perfect continuous staying the same in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Which reporting verb is used for a sentence with an exclamation mark?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'exclaimed' because the book's table changes 'said + exclamation mark' into 'exclaimed' in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: Reshma said, 'I hope I will get admission in the medical college this year.'
options: Reshma hoped that she would get admission in the medical college that year.
Reshma said that she hopes she will get admission this year.
Reshma exclaimed that she would get admission that year.
Reshma wished that she gets admission in the medical college.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the first option because a hope is reported with 'hoped', 'will' becomes 'would', and 'this year' becomes 'that year'.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: 'I have many friends and I have to invite all of them tomorrow,' said Abid.
options: Abid said that he has many friends and invites them tomorrow.
Abid said that he had many friends and that he had to invite all of them the next day.
Abid promised that he had many friends the next day.
Abid said he will invite all of them tomorrow.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the second option because the present tense moves to the past and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' in indirect speech.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: The student said, 'I promise I will do my homework regularly from today.'
options: The student said that he will do his homework from today.
The student hoped that he would do his homework that day.
The student promised that he would do his homework regularly from that day.
The student exclaimed that he does his homework regularly.
mcqs.why: The correct answer uses 'promised' because the book changes 'said + promise' into 'promised', with 'will' becoming 'would' and 'today' becoming 'that day'.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: The blind boy said, 'I wish I could see this interesting match on the television.'
options: The blind boy said that he wishes to see this match.
The blind boy hoped that he can see that match.
The blind boy promised that he could see this match.
The blind boy wished that he could see that interesting match on the television.
mcqs.why: The correct answer uses 'wished' because the book changes 'said + wish' into 'wished', and 'this' becomes 'that' in the reported sentence.

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: 'Our team has won the champion's trophy here for the first time!' said the coach.
options: The coach exclaimed that their team had won the champion's trophy there for the first time.
The coach said that our team has won the trophy here.
The coach wished that their team wins the trophy there.
The coach hoped that the team had won the trophy here.
mcqs.why: The correct answer uses 'exclaimed' because the sentence carries an exclamation mark, the present perfect becomes past perfect, and 'here' becomes 'there'.

mcqs.q: Which reporting verb fits a hope, as in 'We hope we will be able to get permission from our parents,' said the children?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'hoped' because the book's table changes 'said + hope' into 'hoped', giving 'The children hoped that they would be able to get permission from their parents.'

mcqs.q: Change into indirect speech: 'I wish I had ten hands and a hundred fingers to do all this work,' said Feroza.
options: Feroza said that she wishes she has ten hands for this work.
Feroza promised that she had ten hands and a hundred fingers.
Feroza wished that she had ten hands and a hundred fingers to do all that work.
Feroza exclaimed that she will have ten hands for that work.
mcqs.why: The correct answer uses 'wished' because Feroza's sentence is a wish, and in indirect speech 'this work' becomes 'that work'.

lessons.title: Writing: Descriptive Essay and Filling a Simple Form
lessons.notes_html:
Descriptive Essay: Further Practice

A descriptive essay describes a person, place or thing. It includes important details about the person, place or thing in such a manner that the readers can create a picture in their mind about the object being described. In Unit 1 students described a place; in this unit the essay describes a person, in at least four paragraphs, working in pairs, on one of these topics:

  • My favourite Aunt / Uncle
  • A teacher that I remember
  • Our school principal
  • My grandmother / grandfather

After writing, students exchange notebooks with another pair, read each other's essay and give critical feedback, then incorporate the feedback received and rewrite the essay.

Model Essay: My Grandmother (from the solved answers)

My grandmother is the oldest and dearest member of our family. She is about seventy years old. Her hair is white and her face is full of wrinkles, but her smile is always sweet. She wears simple clothes and a white scarf, and she walks slowly with a stick. Her eyes are weak, but her memory is very sharp.

My grandmother is a very kind and patient woman. She never gets angry, even when we make a noise. She tells us stories of her childhood and teaches us good manners. lessons.title: Study Skills: Informal Interviews
lessons.notes_html:
About Informal Interviews

In an interview, one person asks questions to find out some answers, while the other person responds to these questions. Friends sometimes interview each other in an informal manner to understand an issue or problem that one of them is facing. This Study Skills section is for acquiring additional language skills and is not to be formally assessed.

Tips for Conducting an Informal Interview

For the InterviewerFor the Person Giving the Interview
Prepare and ask relevant questionsListen attentively to the question; seek clarification, if needed
Use appropriate reciprocal language effectivelyChoose your words carefully while answering the questions
Take notes and compile the responsesMake sure that the interviewer understands what you are saying
Display appropriate body language and postureUse correct intonation and display appropriate body language

The Money Problem Interview (from the solved answers)

In the dialogue, Student B has been worried ever since his father told him that he cannot pay his fees this year, and he does not know who to talk to. Student A suggests that he could talk to the class teacher, that someone may be able to help, and that he should talk to the principal and ask for more time to pay his fees, assuring him that he will be able to arrange something.

The Fever Interview: Questions, Notes and Report

  • Questions: Since when have you had this fever? Have you seen a doctor or taken any medicine? Do you feel any other symptoms, like headache or body pain? What should we do to help you?
  • Notes: My friend has had severe fever since yesterday. He has not seen a doctor yet. He also has a headache and body pain. We advised him to see a doctor at once and to take rest.
  • Report: My friend has been suffering from severe fever since yesterday, with headache and body pain. He has not yet seen a doctor. We advised him to see a doctor and take complete rest.

Remember

The full task pattern is: prepare three to four questions, interview your partner, prepare notes from the answers, and then report to the class.

lessons.title: Fun: Vocabulary Building
lessons.notes_html:
About the Activity

The Fun section is for having fun with language and is not to be formally assessed. In this vocabulary building activity, students work in groups of four. The teacher puts one word on the board, and each group has to write a new word beginning with the last alphabet (letter) of the previous word.

Rules of the Word Chain

  • Each new word must begin with the last letter of the previous word.
  • Words cannot be repeated; a word can be used only once.
  • Every word should have a minimum of four letters.
  • The group with the most correct words is declared the winner.
  • The groups get ten minutes to do the task.

The Book's Example

chain (ends in 'n') → number (begins with 'n', ends in 'r') → ring (begins with 'r', ends in 'g') → grow → elephant → think. The book explains: the last alphabet in 'chain' is 'n', so the next word has to begin with 'n' - 'number'; its last alphabet is 'r', so the next word begins with 'r' - 'ring', and so on.

Steps to Follow

StepWhat to Do
1Work in groups of four
2Select the person who will write the words on the paper
3Also decide who will go and read the words
4Take a piece of paper
5Write the names of all four group members on it
6Copy the word that the teacher writes on the board
7Start writing the words
8Make sure every group member participates

A Model Chain (from the solved answers)

chain → number → ring → grow → elephant → think → health → house → eagle → energy → yellow → window → water → river → rain → nest → teacher → room → mango → orange → goat → tree → evening → garden → night → tiger → rice → train → nose → exam → music → chair.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: The Role of Women in Pakistan's Creation and Development
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

The reading text is The Role of Women in Pakistan's Creation and Development. Sana is worried because she does not have a computer for gathering information. Her group uses the IDEAL tool to plan their work. The group has six students: Sana, Aliya, Sameer, Ahmad, Razia and Hania. They gather information from a laptop and the internet, newspapers and magazines, and books and a smart phone. They do not use radio and television.

The IDEAL Tool

  • I - Identify: identify the problem.
  • D - Define: define what exactly we want to do to solve the problem.
  • E - Explore: find out as much as we can about how to solve it.
  • A - Action: take the best possible action to try and solve it.
  • L - Look back: look back to see whether the problem has been solved or not.

Five Famous Women

WomanBorn - DiedMain Contribution
Fatima Jinnah1893 - 1969Supported Quaid-e-Azam for about 28 years in the struggle for Pakistan; titled Madr-e-Millat, Mother of the Nation
Begum Jahan Ara Shahnawaz1896 - 1979Represented Muslim women at the three Round Table Conferences in London; first woman to speak in London's Guild Hall
Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan1905 - 1990Organised the women's National Guards of 2400 girls with the rank of Brigadier; founded APWA, the All Pakistan Women Association
Professor Anita Ghulam Ali1934 - 2014Twice Sindh Minister of Education; founding manager of the Sindh Education Foundation
Bilquis Bano Edhiborn 1947Heads the Edhi Foundation with shelter homes and ambulance services; awarded Hilal-e-Imtiaz; called the mother of Pakistan

Key Points

  • Muslim women benefited from Fatima Jinnah's support because through her they could interview Mohammad Ali Jinnah and seek his guidance.
  • Begum Ra'ana worked as a secretary because the Muslim League could not afford a secretary's salary at that time.
  • Begum Jahan Ara could explain the Muslims' point of view in many countries because she travelled widely.
  • Anita Ghulam Ali received the Pride of Performance and Sitara-e-Imtiaz for her tremendous contribution to education.
  • Bilquis Edhi received Hilal-e-Imtiaz for her tireless efforts for the betterment of society.
  • At the end, three students shared their dreams: Maryam wanted to be an educationist to improve female education, Hira, and Daniyal, who wanted to be like Abdul Sattar Edhi and help all human beings in trouble.

Vocabulary

  • opinions - views, what one thinks
  • access - the ability to reach or use something
  • simultaneously - at the same time
  • rehearsed - practised
  • contribution - the part played in bringing something about
  • philanthropist - one who helps others with money and time
  • renowned - famous
  • recognition - acknowledgement, public honour
  • tireless - never tiring
  • inspired - encouraged by someone or something
  • enthusiasm - strong interest and excitement

lessons.title: Listening and Speaking: Asking for and Expressing Preferences by Giving Reasons
lessons.notes_html:
Focus of the Lesson

Unit 6.2 teaches asking for and expressing preferences by giving reasons. Students work in groups of four, and each student takes the role of one character. The role-play scene is about study leave: friends discuss how to plan their studies so they can revise all subjects effectively and be well prepared for the exams. They all want some independent study time and some group study time, and they must remember to disagree politely.

The Model Dialogue

  • Tariq says he does not understand why anyone wants to study so early in the morning; he finds it very hard.
  • Saira gives a reason: she is quite used to waking up early for school, so she wants to continue the same routine during the study holidays.
  • Adnan agrees, because that is the time the mind is fresh after a good night's sleep.
  • Zohair continues the dialogue.

Useful Sentence Patterns

PatternExample from the Model Answer
I prefer ... because ...I prefer studying after lunch, because in the morning I feel sleepy.
I like ... because ...I like studying in my own room, because it is quiet.
I think we should ... because ...I think we should study together in the evening, because then we can help each other with difficult questions.
I would like to ... because ...I would like to revise English first, because I find it the hardest.

Remember

  • Always give a reason after your preference; use the word because.
  • Disagree politely, for example: I disagree politely, or That is a good idea, but I prefer...
  • In the model answer the friends agree in the end: mornings for independent study and evenings for group study.
  • Adnan prefers to revise Science first because it has the most chapters.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Synonyms
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Synonym?

A synonym is a word or phrase that means almost or nearly the same as another word or phrase in the same language. For example, shut is a synonym of close. Synonyms can sometimes replace each other, but many times they cannot; it depends on the context of their use. The teacher's note warns: while many words may seem correct, only one word is the correct synonym in the given context.

Exercise 1: Synonyms in Sentences

WordCorrect SynonymExample Sentence
miniaturetinyHe has made a doll house with tiny furniture for every room.
difficulthardMrs Amjad gave the class a hard assignment for chemistry.
oldelderlyMy grandmother is elderly. She is about 90 years old.
slimthinOur principal is very smart and thin.
stablesteadyA steady government ensures that a nation will progress.
helpassistFarzana is always ready to assist the people in her neighbourhood.
drowsysleepyI feel sleepy after having rice for lunch.
vacantemptyThe house next door has been empty for two years.

Exercise 2: The Right Synonym for the Context

  • weak - This cup of tea tastes like tea flavoured water; it is very weak.
  • important - To succeed in the exams, it is important to study regularly.
  • rough - During the monsoon rains the water in the rivers becomes very rough.
  • old - The ruins of Moen-jo-Daro are old.
  • rich - Pakistan is rich in minerals.
  • valid - Her ID card is no longer valid.
  • real - The bangles are made of real gold.
  • quiet - The students were asked to remain quiet during the test next door.
  • fragrance - This perfume has a lovely fragrance.
  • admiration - The staff was full of admiration for the new manager.

Exercise 3: The Odd Word Out

In each set of five words, four are synonyms and one is different: decent (friendly set), nice (option set), reasonable (rude set), stable (severe set), many (huge set), garden (rubbish set), polite (intelligent set), clean (position set), correct (mistake set) and wound (disease set).

lessons.title: Language Practice: Use of Since and For
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules: Since and For

Since and for are used for similar, but not exactly the same, purposes. Since gives the starting point of actions, events or states continuing until the present. It refers to when things began. It can only be used with the perfect tenses. For is used when we measure the duration, when we say how long something lasts. We can use all verb tenses with for.

WordFollowed ByBook Examples
sincea point in time in the past, until nowI have been waiting since 7 o'clock. I have known him since January. I have been here since 5 o'clock. It has been three years since the last earthquake.
fora period of timeI have known her for a long time. I lived here for ten years. They are exercising for three hours today.

Model Paragraph: My Hobbies

I have been reading story books since I was ten years old, so I have been reading them for nearly six years now. I have been playing cricket since I was eight years old, and I have played it for many years. I still play it every evening because it keeps me healthy and happy. I painted for two years when I was in class six, but I do not paint anymore because I have no time for it.

Remember

  • Ask: does the phrase tell WHEN it began? Use since. Does it tell HOW LONG? Use for.
  • since + 7 o'clock, January, 2020, I was ten years old.
  • for + ten years, three hours, a long time, many years, two years.

mcqs.q: What does SINCE show in a sentence?
options: The starting point of an action continuing until the present
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the starting point, because since refers to when things began and continue until the present.

mcqs.q: What does FOR show in a sentence?
options: The duration, how long something lasts
mcqs.why: The correct answer is duration, because we use for when we measure how long something lasts, like for ten years.

mcqs.q: With which tenses can SINCE be used?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is only the perfect tenses, which is the rule the book gives for the use of since.

mcqs.q: With which tenses can FOR be used?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is all verb tenses, because the book says we can use all verb tenses with for.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: I have been waiting ___ 7 o'clock.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is since, because 7 o'clock is a point in time when the waiting began, and since takes a point in time.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: I have known him ___ January.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is since, because January is the starting point from which the speaker has known him.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: I lived here ___ ten years and then moved to another place.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is for, because ten years is a period of time that measures how long he lived there.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: They are exercising ___ three hours today.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is for, because three hours is a duration, and for is used with a period of time.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: I have been reading story books ___ I was ten years old.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is since, because I was ten years old is the starting point of the reading habit in the model paragraph.

mcqs.q: Complete the sentence: I painted ___ two years when I was in class six.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is for, because two years tells how long the painting lasted, and duration takes for, not since.

lessons.title: Writing: Narrative Essay and Summary Writing
lessons.notes_html:
Narrative Essay: Further Practice

As discussed in Unit 2.4, a narrative essay focuses on telling a story. It includes important details about the incident, such as: when and where the event or incident took place; what happened, with significant details; and what its significance is at the personal, societal and country level. In Exercise 1, students work in groups of three, think of one important event each, share their stories, select one story, and write a report like newspaper reporters, following the steps in Unit 2.4.

Model Narrative Report: A Tree Plantation Day in Our Area

Last Sunday, a tree plantation day was held in our area and the whole neighbourhood took part. In the morning, the students gathered in the school ground with small plants. The headmaster opened the event and the chief guest planted the first tree. Then all the students planted trees along the roads and in the park, and the people of the area planted trees in front of their houses. By noon, more than two hundred trees had been planted. In the evening, the headmaster thanked everyone and asked them to look after the new plants. The day taught everyone that trees are the life of the area.

Summary Writing: Further Practice

A summary gives brief information about a topic. The method is: read the passage, underline the main ideas and words in each paragraph, do not include any details, and then use the underlined key words to write the summary in your own brief form.

Model Summary: Helen Keller

Some people cannot see or hear, and some who could once see and hear lose both, yet many are courageous. Helen Keller was born in 1880 in a small town of the USA. At the age of two she fell seriously ill in February 1882 and became blind and deaf, but her parents never gave up hope. At seven, Miss Sullivan, who had once been blind herself, began to teach her; at the river bank Helen learnt the word water, and then mountains, rivers, history, geography and counting. At eight she went to a school for blind children and regained her speech by ten by feeling her teacher's lip movements. She learnt Braille, passed all her exams, and graduated from Harvard University. In 1956 she visited Pakistan at seventy-six, encouraged deaf and blind people, visited the school for the deaf, dumb and blind in Karachi, and praised the volunteers.

mcqs.q: What does a narrative essay focus on?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is telling a story, because the book says a narrative essay focuses on telling a story about an incident.

mcqs.q: Which detail must a narrative essay include?
options: When and where the event took place
mcqs.why: The correct answer is when and where the event took place, one of the important details the book lists for a narrative essay.

mcqs.q: At which levels should the significance of the event be shown?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the personal, societal and country level, which is how the book asks for the significance of the incident.

mcqs.q: In Exercise 1, students imagine they are what?
options: Newspaper reporters writing a report for publication
mcqs.why: The correct answer is newspaper reporters, because the exercise asks students to report an important event for a newspaper.

mcqs.q: In the model report, how many trees were planted by noon?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is more than two hundred trees, which the model report says were planted by noon on the plantation day.

mcqs.q: What does a summary give about a topic?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is brief information, because the book defines a summary as giving brief information about a topic.

mcqs.q: What is the first step in writing the Helen Keller summary?
options: Underline the main ideas and words in each paragraph
mcqs.why: The correct answer is underlining the main ideas and words in each paragraph, without including any details.

mcqs.q: When and how did Helen Keller become blind and deaf?
options: In February 1882, after falling seriously ill at age two
mcqs.why: The correct answer is February 1882, when little Helen fell seriously ill at the age of two and became blind and deaf.

mcqs.q: Who taught Helen Keller, and what was special about her?
options: Miss Sullivan, who had once been blind and regained her sight
Her mother, who was a doctor
Her father, who ran a school
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Miss Sullivan, who had once been blind herself and regained her sight before teaching Helen.

mcqs.q: How did Helen Keller learn to read, and where did she graduate from?
options: By listening to the radio; Oxford
Through Braille; she graduated from Harvard University
By lip reading only; a school in Karachi
Through pictures; a college in London
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Braille and Harvard University, because Helen learnt to read Braille, passed all exams and graduated from Harvard.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Writing an Article Based on Points
lessons.notes_html:
Writing an Article Based on Points

Very often we note down points when listening to a speech or a lecture. Later, we sometimes need to write that information in the form of a report or an essay. Unit 6.5 gives a table of points about two mountains, K2 and Nanga Parbat, and the task is to turn the points into full essays. This section is for acquiring additional language skills and is not to be formally assessed.

Key Points Table

ItemK2Nanga Parbat
LocationPakistan-China border, between Gilgit in Gilgit-Baltistan and the Tashkurgan Tajik Autonomous County of Xinjiang, ChinaNorthern Areas of Pakistan, between Chilas and Astore, in Diamer
Height28,253 feet (8,612 meters)8,126 meters (26,660 feet)
Mountain RangeKarakoramHimalayas
World RankingSecond-highest in the worldNinth highest in the world
Ranking in PakistanHighestSecond highest
Common NameK2 given in 1852 by T. G. Montgomerie; later Mount Godwin-AustenLiteral meaning: Naked Mountain

Model Essay Facts: K2

  • K2 is called the Savage Mountain for its severe weather and high death rate.
  • Its local names are Chogori, meaning large mountain, and Qogir, meaning Great Mountain.
  • The summit was first reached on July 31, 1954, by Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli of Italy.
  • The first Pakistani, Ashraf Aman, reached K2 on August 9, 1977.
  • K2 is usually climbed in June, July or August and had never been climbed in winter (till the time of the book).

Model Essay Facts: Nanga Parbat

  • It is called the Killer Mountain, as 31 people died trying to climb it before its first ascent.
  • Its local names are Diamer or Deo Mir, meaning huge mountain.
  • The summit was first reached on July 3, 1953, by the Austrian climber Hermann Buhl.
  • The first successful winter climb was on February 26, 2016, by Ali Sadpara, Alex Txikon and Simone Moro.

How to Write

Start with a general opening about Pakistan's mountains, then write one point after another in full sentences in a logical order: location, height, range, ranking, name, climbing history, and a closing line such as: K2 is one of the greatest glories of Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Why do we need to write an article based on points?
options: Points noted from a speech or lecture may later need to be written as a report or essay
Points are only for drawing pictures
Points are used only in exams
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that points noted from a speech or lecture may later need to be written as a report or essay, as the book explains.

mcqs.q: Where does K2 stand?
options: On the Pakistan-China border, between Gilgit and the Tashkurgan Tajik Autonomous County of Xinjiang
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Pakistan-China border between Gilgit and Tashkurgan, which is the location given in the points table.

mcqs.q: What is the height of K2?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 28,253 feet (8,612 meters), the height of K2 given in the table and the model essay.

mcqs.q: To which mountain range does K2 belong?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Karakoram range, and the letter K in K2 also stands for Karakoram.

mcqs.q: What is K2's ranking in the world and in Pakistan?
options: Second-highest in the world and highest in Pakistan
Ninth in the world and second in Pakistan
Highest in the world and in Pakistan
Third in the world and highest in Pakistan
mcqs.why: The correct answer is second-highest in the world and highest in Pakistan, as the points table shows.

mcqs.q: Who gave the name K2, and in which year?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is T. G. Montgomerie in 1852, with K for Karakoram and 2 for the second highest peak.

mcqs.q: What does the name Nanga Parbat literally mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Naked Mountain, which is the literal meaning of Nanga Parbat given in the table.

mcqs.q: What is the height of Nanga Parbat?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8,126 meters (26,660 feet), the height of Nanga Parbat in the Himalayas.

mcqs.q: Who first reached the summit of K2, and when?
options: Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli, on July 31, 1954
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Compagnoni and Lacedelli on July 31, 1954, the first successful climb of K2 recorded in the essay.

mcqs.q: Why is Nanga Parbat called the Killer Mountain?
options: Because 31 people died trying to climb it before its first ascent
Because it is the highest mountain
mcqs.why: The correct answer is because 31 people died trying to climb it before its first ascent, which earned it the name Killer Mountain.

lessons.title: Fun: Doing Something Different
lessons.notes_html:
Doing Something Different

The Fun section is for having fun with language and is not to be formally assessed. Think of one thing you would like to do when you grow up. Think of doing something different, something that people do not normally do. The teacher's note says the purpose is to learn English through fun and enjoyment, and students should think outside the box, for example carving a scene on a stone, making a new toy for young children, or inventing a time machine.

What You Must State

  • What you will do
  • Why you want to do it
  • How you will do it

How to Present It

Take a piece of paper and show what you will do, why you will do it, and how. You can write, draw or use pictures. Use colour pencils or other colours. Make your presentation bright and colourful. After you have done it, share your dream with the rest of the class by showing them your paper presentation. The page has a presentation box with three spaces labelled what, why and how.

Model Answer

  • What: I will open a free library for children in my village.
  • Why: Many children in my village have no books to read. I want them to love reading and to learn new things.
  • How: I will collect old books from friends and elders. I will keep them in a small room in my house. I will ask my teachers to help me arrange the books. I will open the library every evening.

Remember

A good Fun answer is different from normal plans, gives a clear reason, and explains the steps of how the dream will be done.

mcqs.q: What does the Fun section ask you to think of?
options: One thing you would like to do when you grow up, something different that people do not normally do
The marks you want in exams
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one different thing you would like to do when you grow up, something people do not normally do.

mcqs.q: Which three things must you state about your idea?
options: What you will do, why you want to do it, and how you will do it
mcqs.why: The correct answer is what you will do, why you want to do it, and how you will do it, the three points listed in the book.

mcqs.q: How can you show your idea on the paper?
options: By writing, drawing or using pictures
mcqs.why: The correct answer is by writing, drawing or using pictures, because the book allows all three ways to show the idea.

mcqs.q: How should the presentation be made?
options: Bright and colourful, using colour pencils or other colours
mcqs.why: The correct answer is bright and colourful, because the book says to use colour pencils or other colours and make the presentation bright and colourful.

mcqs.q: What do you do after finishing your paper presentation?
options: Share your dream with the rest of the class by showing them your paper
mcqs.why: The correct answer is share your dream with the rest of the class by showing them your paper presentation.

mcqs.q: In the model answer, what will the student do when grown up?
options: Open a paid bookshop in a city
Open a free library for children in the village
mcqs.why: The correct answer is open a free library for children in the village, which is the what of the model answer.

mcqs.q: In the model answer, why does the student want to open the library?
options: To earn a lot of money
To become famous in the city
Because many children in the village have no books to read and should love reading
mcqs.why: The correct answer is because many children in the village have no books to read, and the student wants them to love reading and learn new things.

mcqs.q: In the model answer, how will the student collect books for the library?
options: Collect old books from friends and elders
Take books from the school without asking
mcqs.why: The correct answer is collect old books from friends and elders, the first step of the how in the model answer.

mcqs.q: When will the model library be opened?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is every evening, because the model answer says the library will open every evening.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of thinking outside the box in the teacher's note?
options: Carving a scene on a stone
mcqs.why: The correct answer is carving a scene on a stone, one of the teacher's examples along with making a new toy and inventing a time machine.

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: The Secret of Success
lessons.notes_html:
Summary

A long time ago a king searched for the secret of success. He believed that if he found the answers to three questions, he would discover the secret and never fail. He thought for many days, but the answers evaded him, so he asked others in order.

The Three Questions

  • What is the most important time to start something?
  • What is the most important work to do?
  • Who is the most important person?

The king asked first himself, then his ministers, his courtiers, the scholars and wise men, the common people (with a reward of 5000 gold coins), and finally the saint. The wise and learned men could not agree and argued among themselves, so none of their answers satisfied him.

About the Saint and the Bearded Man

The saint was an old wise man who lived all alone in a jungle. He mixed only with the poor and needy and did not like meeting wealthy people, so the king dressed in rags, went alone, and told his servants not to follow. The saint was old and weak, breathing hard and stopping frequently to rest. A bearded man who had come to kill the king, and who had been injured by the king's servants, ran towards the king and fainted because he was seriously wounded. The king himself picked him up and bandaged his wounds, stayed the night because he was tired and it was dark, and saved the man's life. The bearded man then became one of the king's most faithful servants. The saint told the king that all his questions had been answered through the events of the day.

Key Points: The Secret of Success

QuestionAnswer from the story
Most important timeThe present
Most important workWhat you are doing now
Most important personThe person you are with at the moment

The lesson applies to all people, not only the king: we cannot change the past, the future is not in our hands, so we should do our present work well and help and respect the people around us.

Vocabulary

Word / PhraseMeaning
discoverfind out
evadedescaped, avoided
disappointedsad because hopes were not fulfilled
consultask for advice
ponderedthought deeply
destitutevery poor
frequentlyoften
determinedfirm, decided
glancedlooked quickly
straight awayat once
hospitalitykind welcome to guests
break of daydawn, early morning
bitterfull of hatred
griefdeep sorrow
count on medepend on me
departedleft

Remember

Order in which the king asked: 1 King himself, 2 Ministers, 3 Courtiers, 4 Scholars and wise men, 5 Common people, 6 Saint. The statement that best summarises the story is: the present is the most important time.

mcqs.q: How many questions did the king want answered?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three questions, because the king believed their answers would reveal the secret of success.

mcqs.q: Why did the king want the answers to the three questions?
options: To discover the secret of success and never fail
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to discover the secret of success and never fail, which was the king's purpose from the start of the story.

mcqs.q: Who was asked FIRST after the king himself?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the ministers, who come second in the order: king himself, ministers, courtiers, scholars, common people, saint.

mcqs.q: Who was asked LAST by the king?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the saint, the wise old man in the jungle, who was sixth and last in the order the king consulted.

mcqs.q: Why could the wise and learned men not satisfy the king?
options: They could not see eye to eye and argued among themselves
They had never met the king
They asked for more gold coins
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they could not see eye to eye with each other and ended up arguing, so no answer satisfied the king.

mcqs.q: Why did the king dress in rags to meet the saint?
options: Because the saint mixed only with the poor and he wanted to appear poor and destitute
Because his own clothes were torn
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the saint mixed only with the poor and needy, so the king dressed in rags to appear poor and destitute.

mcqs.q: How did the king go to see the saint?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is all alone, because the king told his servants not to go with him so he would appear poor and destitute.

mcqs.q: Who warned the king that the bearded man was coming?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the saint, who warned the king before the wounded bearded man reached him.

mcqs.q: Why was the bearded man running towards the king?
options: He had come to kill the king
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that he had come to kill the king, though he fainted from his serious wounds before he could do so.

mcqs.q: Why did the bearded man become the king's loyal servant?
options: The saint ordered him to serve
The king gave him gold coins
The king had saved his life by caring for him and bandaging his wounds
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the king saved his life by caring for him and bandaging his wounds, so he became a faithful servant.

mcqs.q: Which statement best summarises the story?
options: The present is not what matters
The present gives you the most joy
The past has all the answers
The present is the most important time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the present is the most important time, which is the central lesson the saint's day of events taught the king.

mcqs.q: What does 'pondered' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is thought deeply, as in the king pondering over his three questions for many days.

mcqs.q: What does 'destitute' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is very poor, which is why the king dressed in rags to appear destitute before the saint.

mcqs.q: What does the phrase 'break of day' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is dawn or early morning, while hospitality means kind welcome and grief means deep sorrow.

mcqs.q: What does 'count on me' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is depend on me, meaning you can trust and rely on me in every difficulty.

lessons.title: Listening and Speaking: Conventions of Public Speaking
lessons.notes_html:
About This Section

Unit 7.2 teaches the simple conventions of public speaking. Students work in groups of six and prepare a two-minute speech. Exercise 1 topics are: Water problem, Electricity shortage, Sewerage system, Waste disposal, Education system, Health Facilities, 14th August, Literacy day, Plantation and Wild Life Protection. Exercise 2 is a two-minute speech for the school assembly on: Cheating, Regularity and punctuality, Discipline, Cleanliness, Games and sports, or Team work.

How to Prepare: Step 1 and Step 2

  • Step 1 (15 minutes): Discuss one topic at a time. Brainstorm for ideas, remembering you have only two minutes to speak.
  • Identify the focus: decide which aspect you want to cover.
  • Organise your ideas: think which point will come first, second, and so on.
  • For each point, have supporting details: examples, quotes, facts and figures to explain your point.
  • Step 2: Prepare six chits, each with one topic. Each member picks one chit and prepares a two-minute speech from the discussion; you may add other points.

How to Deliver: Step 3

  • Introduce yourself.
  • Introduce the topic.
  • Tell your group members briefly what you are going to talk about.
  • State point 1, explain, give examples and reasons; then point 2 and point 3 in the same way.
  • Conclude your topic by briefly restating your main points.
  • Try to give an idea, suggestion or your viewpoint as the last statement.
  • Other members listen, provide positive feedback and suggest ways the speaker could improve.

Remember While Speaking

  • Maintain eye contact with the audience.
  • Use appropriate gestures, but do so naturally; do not overdo them.
  • Do not read from a paper; you may have cue cards with some points. Cue cards are small cards on which only the main points, not whole sentences, are written, numbered in the order they are to be used.
  • Use appropriate tone, pauses and stresses, as this allows the listeners to understand your point better.

Model Speech Opening

The model speeches begin with a greeting and self-introduction, for example: Assalam-o-Alaikum. My name is Ali, and today I will speak on plantation (or cleanliness). The speaker then gives a first point, a second point and a third point, and ends with a conclusion beginning In conclusion.

mcqs.q: How long should each speech in Unit 7.2 be?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is two minutes, and Step 1 reminds speakers to brainstorm knowing they have only two minutes to speak.

mcqs.q: In Exercise 1, students work in groups of how many?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is groups of six, and in Step 2 six chits are prepared so each member picks one topic.

mcqs.q: What is the FIRST thing to do in Step 1?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is brainstorm for ideas, before identifying the focus and organising the points in order.

mcqs.q: What should support each point in a speech?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is examples, quotes, facts and figures, because each point needs supporting details to explain it clearly.

mcqs.q: What are cue cards?
options: Cards with the full speech written on them
Small cards with only the main points, numbered in order of use
Cards used to vote for topics
mcqs.why: The correct answer is small cards with only the main points, not whole sentences, numbered so they do not get mixed up.

mcqs.q: What should a speaker do FIRST when delivering the speech?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is introduce yourself, then introduce the topic and briefly say what you are going to talk about.

mcqs.q: How should a speech end?
options: By briefly restating the main points and giving an idea, suggestion or viewpoint last
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to conclude by briefly restating the main points and giving an idea, suggestion or viewpoint as the last statement.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct point to remember while speaking?
options: Maintain eye contact with the audience
mcqs.why: The correct answer is maintain eye contact with the audience, along with natural gestures and appropriate tone, pauses and stresses.

mcqs.q: What should listeners do after a group member delivers a speech?
options: Provide positive feedback and suggest ways to improve
Choose a new topic at once
mcqs.why: The correct answer is provide positive feedback and suggest ways in which the speaker could improve, as Step 3 directs.

mcqs.q: Which list contains ONLY Exercise 2 assembly topics?
options: 14th August, Literacy day, Wild Life Protection
Health Facilities, Sewerage system, Waste disposal
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Cheating, Discipline, Cleanliness and Team work, which are assembly topics; the others belong to Exercise 1.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Translation
lessons.notes_html:
Key Rule of Translation

Translating from one language to another requires special skills. One cannot translate word for word, as words take different meanings in different contexts, even in the same language. When translating, first see what meaning is coming out in the sentence, then translate accordingly.

One Word, Many Meanings: spring

SentenceMeaning of spring
I will go to Murree in spring.the season
There is a spring of hot water at Manghopir, in Karachi.a natural fountain of water
Since a spring is broken, this clock is not working.a coiled metal part
With a spring, the runner crossed the winning line.a jump

Words That Change Meaning and Word Class

WordMeanings in Exercise 1
trainrailway train (noun); to give training (verb)
lightbrightness (noun); to kindle (verb)
bookto reserve (verb); a book (noun)
stateto say, express (verb); the country (noun)
pointopinion, view (noun); to show with the finger (verb)
rankposition (noun); post, grade (noun)

Figurative Language: Literal vs Real Meaning

In figurative language, the meaning of the words or expressions used is different from the literal meaning. A literal translation of She has a sweet tooth (a tooth that is sweet) makes no sense; its real meaning is She loves sweet things. This news is music to my ears really means I am very pleased to hear this news.

  • The sun peaked happily from behind the clouds = The sun appeared from behind the clouds.
  • The trees danced back and forth in the wind = The trees swayed in the wind.
  • The bell refused to ring = The bell did not ring.
  • The angry sky roared = The sky thundered and lightning flashed.
  • Such a chicken = so cowardly; all brains = all very clever; guardian angel = protector and helper; on cloud nine = very happy.

Remember

Always translate the meaning that fits the context and bring out the real meaning of figurative sentences, never the word-for-word literal meaning.

mcqs.q: What is the main rule of translation taught in this unit?
options: Words take different meanings in different contexts, so translate by context
Figurative sentences have no real meaning
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that words take different meanings in different contexts, so one cannot translate word for word.

mcqs.q: In 'I will go to Murree in spring', what does 'spring' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the season, because the sentence is about going to Murree at a time of year.

mcqs.q: In 'There is a spring of hot water at Manghopir', what does 'spring' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a natural fountain of water, because the sentence describes hot water coming from the ground at Manghopir.

mcqs.q: In 'Since a spring is broken, this clock is not working', what does 'spring' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a coiled metal part, because a clock works with a coiled spring inside it.

mcqs.q: In 'I can train you to become a good cricketer', what does 'train' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to give training, used as a verb here, unlike the noun in 'The train left the station'.

mcqs.q: In 'Please, light all the candles', what does 'light' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to kindle, used as a verb, while in 'plenty of light in this room' light is the noun meaning brightness.

mcqs.q: In 'The state should ensure that all people follow the rules', what does 'state' mean?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the country, used as a noun, while in 'state their reasons' state is a verb meaning to say or express.

mcqs.q: What is the REAL meaning of 'She has a sweet tooth'?
options: She has a tooth that is sweet
mcqs.why: The correct answer is she loves sweet things, because the literal meaning about a sweet tooth makes no sense in translation.

mcqs.q: What is the real meaning of 'I've been on cloud nine all day'?
options: I have been travelling all day
I have been very happy all day
I have been sleeping all day
I have been watching clouds all day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is I have been very happy all day, because on cloud nine is figurative language for great happiness.

mcqs.q: What does 'You are my guardian angel' really mean?
options: You can fly like an angel
You are my protector and helper
mcqs.why: The correct answer is you are my protector and helper, which is the real, figurative meaning given in the exercise.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Prefixes (Continued)
lessons.notes_html:
What Is a Prefix?

We sometimes add a pair or a group of letters (the book says alphabets) at the beginning of a word to add something to the meaning of the word. As discussed in Unit 4.3, these are called prefixes. In this unit the prefixes un-, in- and dis- are practised, and each one gives the new word a negative or opposite meaning.

Prefix un-

Base wordWith un-Use in the exercise
healthyunhealthyAn unhealthy person often falls sick.
friendlyunfriendlySaba is very unfriendly and does not like meeting people.
gratefulungratefulPeople who are ungrateful never thank others for helping them.
happyunhappyBadar was very unhappy because he lost his favourite watch.
wiseunwiseMy uncle took an unwise decision due to which he suffered a big loss.

Prefix in-

Base wordWith in-Use in the exercise
activeinactiveThis small boy is very inactive and does not take part in any work.
correctincorrectThe judge was upset with the prisoner for giving an incorrect statement.
completeincompleteDo not leave your work incomplete or the boss will be angry.
attentiveinattentiveSajid is very inattentive in class; hence, he often fails in the tests.
sufficientinsufficientThis amount of money is insufficient if you want to buy a new computer.

Prefix dis-

Base wordWith dis-Use in the exercise
agreedisagreeWe sometimes disagree even with our very close friends.
honestdishonestWe cannot trust dishonest people as they can cheat us.
obedientdisobedientA disobedient child can cause many problems for the whole family.
satisfieddissatisfiedOur teacher was dissatisfied with our performance in the competition.
loyaldisloyalWe should never be disloyal to our country.

Remember

Choose the prefix that fits the base word given in the exercise: un- with happy, friendly, wise, healthy, grateful; in- with correct, sufficient, active, attentive, complete; dis- with satisfied, obedient, honest, loyal, agree.

mcqs.q: What is a prefix?
options: Letters added at the end of a word
A pair or group of letters added at the beginning of a word to add to its meaning
A word with the same meaning
The middle part of a word
mcqs.why: The correct answer is letters added at the beginning of a word, which add something to the meaning of the word.

mcqs.q: 'An ____ person often falls sick.' Choose the correct word.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is unhealthy, formed with un- plus healthy, because a person who is not healthy often falls sick.

mcqs.q: 'Saba is very ____ and does not like meeting people.' Choose the correct word.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is unfriendly, formed with un- plus friendly, because Saba does not like meeting people.
