lessons.title: Writing: Compare and Contrast Essay and Informal Emails
lessons.notes_html:
Compare and Contrast Essay: Further Practice

In Unit 7.4 students revisit the tips on writing a compare and contrast essay given in Unit 3.4 and read the sample essay again. A compare and contrast essay shows how two things are alike (compare) and how they are different (contrast). The two topics are: Reading story books and reading course books, and What happens when a school has a good principal or a bad one. Partners exchange their essays and provide critical feedback.

Model Essay 1: Story Books and Course Books

Both story books and course books are read by students, and both increase knowledge. However, they are different in many ways. Story books are read for pleasure; they take us to new worlds, teach us about people and places, and improve our language in a happy way. Course books are read for study; they contain the lessons we must learn for our exams and must be read with care and attention. Story books are chosen by the reader, but course books are fixed by the school. All in all, both kinds of books are needed: course books help us pass our exams, and story books make us love reading and learning. Note the linking phrases: Both ... and, However, On the other hand, All in all.

Model Essay 2: A Good Principal and a Bad One

Both a good principal and a bad principal hold the same office, but their schools are very different. A good principal comes on time, checks the classes, helps the teachers and listens to the students; his school is clean, classes are regular and results are good. A bad principal comes late, does not check the classes and does not listen to anyone; the teachers are careless and the students are unhappy. All in all, a good principal makes a school a garden, and a bad principal makes it a desert.

Informal Emails: Letter vs Email

LetterEmail
Written on paperWritten on a computer or phone and sent over the internet
Full address and date at the topTo, Cc and Subject lines instead
Takes days to reachReaches at once
Usually longer and more formalUsually short, brief and informal
Ends with a signatureEnds with the sender's name

Model Informal Emails

Email 1 (requesting help): To and Subject: help with maths homework. Hi Ali, I hope you are well. I am finding the maths homework very difficult, especially the questions on fractions. Will you please help me with it tomorrow after school? Your friend, Ahmed. Email 2 (suggesting free-time activity): Subject: let's play cricket on Sunday. The writer suggests playing cricket on Sunday morning and asks the friend to tell if he is free. An informal email to a class fellow is friendly, short and brief.

mcqs.q: What does a compare and contrast essay show?
options: Only the history of two things
How two things are alike and how they are different
Only the differences between two things
mcqs.why: The correct answer is how two things are alike and how they are different, as both model essays compare and then contrast their two subjects.

mcqs.q: In the model essay, what is COMMON to story books and course books?
options: Both are chosen by the reader
Both are read only for pleasure

Both are fixed by the school
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that both are read by students and both increase knowledge, which is the comparison point opening the essay.

mcqs.q: How are story books different from course books in the model essay?
options: Course books are read for pleasure
Story books are fixed by the school
Story books are read for pleasure, course books are read for study
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that story books are read for pleasure while course books are read for study for exams, the main contrast in the essay.

mcqs.q: Which phrase is used in the model essays to sum up at the end?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is All in all, used in both model essays to begin the concluding summing-up sentence.

mcqs.q: After completing a compare and contrast essay with a partner, students should:
options: Exchange work, read each other's work and provide critical feedback
mcqs.why: The correct answer is exchange work and provide critical feedback, as Exercise 2 of Unit 7.4 instructs partners to do.

options: An email takes days to reach
An email reaches at once, a letter takes days
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that an email reaches at once while a letter takes days to reach its reader.

mcqs.q: What appears at the top of an email instead of a full address and date?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is To, Cc and Subject lines, which replace the full address and date written at the top of a letter.

mcqs.q: How does an email usually end, compared with a letter?
options: An email ends with the sender's name; a letter ends with a signature
An email ends with a signature; a letter ends with a name
Both end with a full address
An email has no ending at all
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that an email ends with the sender's name while a letter ends with a signature, one of the noted differences.

mcqs.q: Which is a correct topic for the informal email in Exercise 4?
options: Requesting help with school work you find difficult
mcqs.why: The correct answer is requesting help with school work you find difficult, one of the two given choices for the email to a class fellow.

mcqs.q: What is the tone and length of an informal email, as noted in the differences?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is short, brief and informal, unlike a letter which is usually longer and more formal.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Creative Writing
lessons.notes_html:
About This Section

Unit 7.5 Study Skills is for acquiring additional language skills and is not to be formally assessed. The creative writing work is built on the poem Abou Ben Adhem by James Henry Leigh Hunt. Students first read the poem silently, then recite it in groups of four, one student reading one verse each.

The Poem: Abou Ben Adhem

Abou Ben Adhem awoke one night from a deep dream of peace and saw, within the moonlight in his room, an Angel writing in a book of gold. Exceeding peace had made Ben Adhem bold, and he asked, What writest thou? The Angel answered, The names of those who love the Lord. When Abou asked, And is mine one? the Angel replied, Nay, not so. Abou then said cheerfully, I pray thee, then, write me as one that loves his fellow men. The Angel wrote and vanished. The next night it came again with a great wakening light and showed the names whom love of God had blessed, and Ben Adhem's name led all the rest.

Rhyming Words

Remember: rhyming words may have different spellings but similar sounds. Students find the rhyming pairs from the poem, then think of two other words that rhyme with each pair.

Rhyming words from the poemAdditional rhyming words
increase / peacecheese, geese
room / bloomgloom, groom
gold / boldcold, hold
said / headbed, led
accord / Lordboard, sword
one / so (closing sounds as listed)go, no
then / menwhen, pen
night / lightright, sight
bless'd / restbest, test

Writing Your Own Poem

Working with a partner and using words from the additional rhyming words lists, students write a short poem of at least eight lines. The model begins: My brother and I loved the geese. / We always fed them bread and cheese. / At night we slept in our room, / And dreamed of flowers in full bloom.

Remember

The poem's message is that loving your fellow men is placed highest: Abou asked to be written as one who loves his fellow men, and his name led all the rest.

mcqs.why: The correct answer is room and bloom, from the moonlight in his room making it rich like a lily in bloom.

lessons.title: Fun: Find the Odd One Out
lessons.notes_html:
About This Game

Unit 7.6 Fun is for having fun with language and is not to be formally assessed. Students work in pairs. From each word given in capital letters, many new words can be formed. Out of the six words given, one is wrong: it contains a letter that is either extra or is not there in the main word. Circle the word that is wrong, and add two more words of 4 letters or more. The pair that finishes first will be the winner. A word is also wrong if it uses a letter twice when the main word has it only once.

The Ten Main Words and Their Odd Ones Out

ENDEAVOURrounderuses R twice; main word has R onceover, adore
DISREPUTABLEtabletuses T twice; main word has T oncepearl, usable

Remember

Check every letter of a formed word against the main word: the letter must be present in the main word, and it cannot be used more times than it appears in the main word.

It is written in small letters

lessons.title: Reading Comprehension: Ghazi's Diary
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Ghazi's diary has two entries. Entry 1 (Wednesday, 10th February, 2015) is on 'Village life' and is descriptive: Ghazi remembers the simple village where he lived sixty years ago and compares it with his present city life in Karachi. Entry 2 (Friday, 4th August, 2017) is on 'We Need to Store Rain Water' and is narrative: it tells how rivers flood Pakistan in the monsoon and how barrages like the Guddu Barrage store water and control floods.

Key Points: Entry 1

  • Entry 1 has 7 paragraphs; Entry 2 has 8 paragraphs.
  • Village houses were mud houses of wood, straw and mud, with three rooms and a kitchen; people sat and slept on the floor, so very few people had knee problems.
  • There were no roads, only narrow mud lanes that became slippery in the rainy season, and no vehicles were needed because everything was near.
  • Shopkeepers knew everyone by name and gave goods on credit. Men met at the Otaq and women at the village well to share news and folk songs.
  • The writer is not happy now: he lives in a beautiful house in Karachi but desperately misses his village and wishes for a time machine to go back sixty years.

Key Points: Entry 2 and the Guddu Barrage

PointDetail
Built onThe river Indus
Breadth of river at GudduFourteen kilometres
Flood water that can flow through itAbout 1.2 million cusecs
Main canalsThree: Begari Sindh Feeder and Desert Pat Feeder (right bank), Ghotki Feeder (left bank)
Area irrigated2.7 million acres in Sukkur and Jacobabad (Sindh) and Kalat division (Baluchistan)
People who built itMore than 5000 engineers, technicians and labourers; work started on 4th February, 1962

The main purpose of barrages is to control the flow of water in the flood season, store it, and release it for irrigation through the canals throughout the year. Through proper water management we can grow surplus food, export it and earn foreign exchange.

Vocabulary

WordMeaningWordMeaning
desperatelywith great longingdevastationgreat destruction
siblingsbrothers and sistershavocgreat damage, ruin
commutingtravelling from one place to anothercapturecatch, hold
creditgoods taken now, paid for laterretainkeep
devicesmachines, gadgetsirrigationsupplying water to crops
compromisedweakened, harmedtamedbrought under control
accessthe way to reach or useself-sufficientable to meet one's own needs
replacedtook the place ofsurplusextra, more than needed

Remember

Pakistan's water problems include not enough water for drinking and farming, floods in the rainy season, contaminated drinking water and open defecation spreading germs. Citizens should save water and use latrines; the government should build more barrages to store rain water.

It is on storing rain water, written on Friday, 4th August, 2017
It is on the Guddu Barrage, written in 1962
It is on city life in Karachi, written on Sunday

Houses made only of glass and steel

lessons.title: Listening and Speaking: Conventions of Debates
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 8.2 teaches the simple conventions of debates. A debate is held on a given topic. One pair speaks in favour of the topic and the other pair speaks against it. Each speaker follows a clear order so that the debate stays fair and easy to follow.

Key Points: Rules for the First Pair (in favour)

  • State that you agree with the topic.
  • Give one reason at a time as to why you agree.
  • Support each reason with examples, facts, figures, quotes, etc.
  • Follow up with the next point(s) in the manner stated above.
  • Later, give counter arguments to prove you are right, by giving other examples, facts, figures, quotes, etc. in favour of your point.

Key Points: Rules for the Second Pair (against)

  • State that you disagree with the topic.
  • Give one reason at a time as to why you disagree.
  • Support each reason with examples, facts, figures, quotes, etc.
  • Follow up with the next point(s) in the manner stated above.
  • Pick up on your opponents' point(s) and refute them (prove them wrong) by giving examples, facts, figures, quotes, etc.

How the Class Debate Is Organized

StepDetail
GroupWork in groups of four; form two pairs, Pair A and Pair B
DiscussionDiscuss the topic for 3-4 minutes before the quick debate
Debate time10 minutes for each topic
Second topicThe pairs change sides: the pair that spoke in favour now speaks against, and the other pair speaks in favour
TopicsTopics must be debatable, not one-sided

Remember: The Model Topic

For the topic 'You get respect if you give respect', points in favour are: respect is like a mirror, when you respect others they respect you back; a respectful person wins friends and is liked by all; in a family and in a class, respect keeps peace. Points against are: some people do not return respect; respect must be earned by good actions; and a person should respect himself first.

mcqs.q: What is the first thing the first pair must do in a debate?
options: State that they agree with the topic
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to state that they agree with the topic, because the first pair speaks in favour and begins by stating agreement.

mcqs.q: How many reasons should a speaker give at a time?
options: All the reasons together in one long list
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one reason at a time, because the book's rule says to give one reason at a time as to why you agree or disagree.

mcqs.q: How must each reason in a debate be supported?
options: With examples, facts, figures and quotes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is examples, facts, figures and quotes, because the book says to support each reason in exactly this way.

mcqs.q: What is the first step of the second pair in a debate?
options: Pick up the opponents' points at once
State that they disagree with the topic
State that they agree with the first pair
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to state that they disagree with the topic, because the second pair speaks against the topic and begins by stating disagreement.

mcqs.q: What extra step must the second pair take?
options: Repeat their own first point again
Pick up on the opponents' points and refute them with examples, facts, figures and quotes
mcqs.why: The correct answer is refuting the opponents' points, because the book adds this step for the second pair: prove the opponents wrong with support.

mcqs.q: What does 'refute' mean in the debate rules?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'to prove wrong', because the book itself explains refute in brackets as 'prove them wrong'.

mcqs.q: What do counter arguments do in a debate?
options: They prove you are right by giving other examples, facts, figures and quotes in favour of your point
They end the debate at once
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that counter arguments prove you are right with fresh support, as the book states for the first pair.

mcqs.q: How is the class debate group organized in Exercise 1?
options: In one big circle of the whole class
In groups of four, forming two pairs: Pair A and Pair B
In pairs chosen by the opponents
mcqs.why: The correct answer is groups of four forming two pairs, because Exercise 1 says to form two pairs within the group of four.

mcqs.q: How much time is given for each debate topic?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ten minutes for each topic, because Exercise 1 clearly gives 10 minutes for each topic after 3-4 minutes of discussion.

mcqs.q: Which point supports the topic 'You get respect if you give respect'?
options: A person should respect himself first
Respect must only be earned by good actions
Respect is like a mirror: when you respect others, they respect you back
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the mirror point, because it is listed in favour of the topic: respect given is respect returned.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Degrees of Adverbs
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

Adverbs often tell us how an action was done. Like adjectives, adverbs also have three degrees: positive, comparative and superlative.

  • One-syllable adverbs usually take -er to form the comparative degree and -est to form the superlative degree, e.g. high - higher - highest.
  • Adverbs that have two or more syllables usually form the comparative degree with 'more' and the superlative degree with 'most', e.g. smoothly - more smoothly - most smoothly.
  • Adverbs can have irregular degrees also, e.g. badly - worse - worst, and well - better - best.

Key Points: The Degree Table

PositiveComparativeSuperlative
angrilymore angrilymost angrily
carefullymore carefullymost carefully
earlyearlierearliest
fastfasterfastest
hardharderhardest
highhigherhighest
longlongerlongest
farfartherfarthest
quicklymore quicklymost quickly
wellbetterbest

Remember: Using the Degrees

In Exercise 2 each adverb is used only once: 'My uncle went the farthest from his home during the recent floods'; 'Let's see who runs the fastest in the race'; 'The Bolan Express is the earliest train'; 'Saima answered more quickly than her friends'; 'Newborn babies should be handled more gently than all other age groups.' In the passage of Exercise 3, Salim wanted to perform better than his friends, worked hard, read each section carefully, and submitted his paper happily.

mcqs.q: What are the three degrees of adverbs?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is positive, comparative and superlative, because the book says adverbs, like adjectives, have these three degrees.

mcqs.q: How do one-syllable adverbs usually form their comparative and superlative degrees?
options: With -er for the comparative and -est for the superlative
mcqs.why: The correct answer is -er and -est, because the book gives the example high - higher - highest for one-syllable adverbs.

mcqs.q: How do adverbs of two or more syllables usually form their degrees?
options: With 'more' for the comparative and 'most' for the superlative
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'more' and 'most', because the book gives the example smoothly - more smoothly - most smoothly.

mcqs.q: Which set shows an irregular degree given in the book?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is badly - worse - worst, because the book gives it as the example of an adverb with irregular degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the comparative degree of 'carefully'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'more carefully', because carefully has more than one syllable, so it forms its comparative with 'more'.

mcqs.q: What is the positive degree of the adverb whose superlative is 'fastest'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'fast', because the table gives fast - faster - fastest, so the positive degree is fast.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'As compared to the soldiers in the first and middle rows, the soldiers in the last row fought the enemy ______.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'most bravely', because the sentence compares the last row with all the other rows, so the superlative degree is needed.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Saima answered ______ than her friends.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'more quickly', because 'than' shows a comparison between Saima and her friends, so the comparative degree is used.

mcqs.q: Complete the passage sentence: 'Salim wanted to perform ______ than his friends because he wanted to get the scholarship.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'better', because better is the comparative degree of the irregular adverb well, and the sentence compares Salim with his friends.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'My uncle went the ______ from his home during the recent floods.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'farthest', because 'the' before the blank shows the superlative degree of far: far - farther - farthest.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Suffixes (Additional Practice)
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

We sometimes add a pair or group of letters (the book says 'alphabets') at the end of a word to add something to the meaning of the word. These are called suffixes. We can use suffixes to make many new words, for example, adjectives.

Key Points: The Suffix 'able'

The suffix 'able' makes adjectives that show something can be done: fashion + able = fashionable; laugh + able = laughable.

Word + ableAdjectiveBook example
move + ablemovableWe moved all the movable furniture to one side.
wash + ablewashableTake easily washable clothes when travelling.
comfort + ablecomfortableThis is a very comfortable chair.
punish + ablepunishableNon-payment of taxes is a punishable crime.
cure + ablecurableWe can recover from curable diseases quickly.

Key Points: The Suffix 'less'

The suffix 'less' makes adjectives that show 'without': noise + less = noiseless; power + less = powerless.

Word + lessAdjectiveBook example
taste + lesstastelessThis food is tasteless.
bone + lessbonelessBuy boneless chicken for the new dish.
use + lessuselessThis fellow is useless as far as work is concerned.
job + lessjoblessI found work after being jobless for six months.
home + lesshomelessMany homeless people sleep on the footpaths.

Remember

Both exercises form adjectives: first choose the right base word for the sentence, then add the suffix. Each given word is used only once in the exercise.

mcqs.q: What is a suffix?
options: A pair or group of letters added at the end of a word to add something to its meaning
A word added at the start of a sentence
mcqs.why: The correct answer is letters added at the end of a word, because the book defines suffixes in exactly this way.

mcqs.q: What is 'fashion + able'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'fashionable', because the book gives fashion + able = fashionable as its first example.

mcqs.q: What is 'power + less'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'powerless', because the book gives power + less = powerless as an example of the suffix 'less'.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'We moved all the ______ furniture to one side.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'movable', because move + able = movable, and furniture that can be moved fits the sentence.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'When travelling, we should try and take easily ______ clothes with us.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'washable', because wash + able = washable, and clothes that can be washed easily are best for travelling.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'This is a very ______ chair.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'comfortable', because comfort + able = comfortable, which describes a chair that gives comfort.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Non-payment of taxes is a ______ crime.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'punishable', because punish + able = punishable, meaning a crime for which one can be punished.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'We can recover from ______ diseases quickly if we go to the doctor.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'curable', because cure + able = curable, and only curable diseases allow a quick recovery.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'This food is ______ as compared to the food we had yesterday.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'tasteless', because taste + less = tasteless, meaning the food has no taste.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 'Many ______ people sleep on the footpaths.'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'homeless', because home + less = homeless, and people without homes sleep on the footpaths.

lessons.title: Language Practice: Quotation Marks
lessons.notes_html:
Grammar Rules

In writing, words that are actually used by speakers are put in quotation marks. They are put in before the first word spoken and after the last spoken word. The spoken words can be at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end of the sentence. The closing quotation mark is always put after a punctuation mark, i.e. a comma, full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark.

Key Points: Book Examples

  • "Have you finished your homework, Zahid?" asked his mother.
  • "I can do my work later," replied Zahid.
  • His father said, "You will not be allowed to go out until you finish your homework," and went out of the room.
  • Zahid was upset but he said, "Okay, I will finish my homework and then go."

Key Points: Correcting the Exercise Sentences

SentenceCorrect form
Speech at the start"We are going to be late for school, Amjad," said his sister.
Speech at the endThe students stood up and said, "Good morning, teacher."
Speech in the middleThe cleaner said, "I have cleaned your yard," and then he went away.
Speech broken in two"Come on in, children," said the gatekeeper, "I am going to close the gate."
Two spoken sentences"I have lost my car keys," said the old man. "How can I start my car now?"

Remember: The Story 'Frogs'

In Exercise 5, quotation marks, capital letters, full stops and commas are added to the story 'Frogs'. A bunch of tiny frogs arranged a running competition to reach the top of a very high tower. The crowd shouted negative things like "It is too difficult! No one will make it!" One frog reached the top because the winner was deaf and could not hear them. The wisdom of the story is: never listen to other people when they are being negative or pessimistic, and always say, "With God's help I can do this."

mcqs.q: Why are quotation marks used in writing?
options: To put in the words that are actually used by speakers
To show the title of every book
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to mark the words actually used by speakers, because the book begins the section with this rule.

mcqs.q: Where are quotation marks placed around spoken words?
options: Before the first word spoken and after the last spoken word
Only after the last spoken word
At the start of the paragraph only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is before the first word and after the last word spoken, because the book states this placement rule.

mcqs.q: Where is the closing quotation mark always put?
options: At the end of the line
After a punctuation mark, such as a comma, full stop, question mark or exclamation mark
mcqs.why: The correct answer is after a punctuation mark, because the teacher's note says the closing quotation mark is always put after a punctuation mark.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: We are going to be late for school, Amjad, said his sister.
"We are going to be late for school, Amjad, said his sister"
We are going "to be late" for school, Amjad, said his sister.
"We are going to be late for school, Amjad," said his sister.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the first option, because the spoken words are inside quotation marks and the comma comes before the closing mark.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: The students stood up and said, "Good morning, teacher."
The students stood up and said, Good morning, teacher.
"The students stood up and said, Good morning", teacher.
The students stood up and said, Good morning, "teacher."
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the second option, because the greeting 'Good morning, teacher.' is the spoken part and takes the quotation marks.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: The cleaner "said, I have cleaned your yard," and then he went away.
The cleaner said, "I have cleaned your yard, and then he went away."
The cleaner said, "I have cleaned your yard," and then he went away.
The cleaner said, I have cleaned your yard, and then he went away.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the last option, because only 'I have cleaned your yard' was spoken; the rest is narration outside the marks.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: "Come on in, children," said the gatekeeper, "I am going to close the gate."
Come on in, children, said the gatekeeper, I am going to close the gate.
"Come on in, children, said the gatekeeper, I am going to close the gate."
Come on in, "children," said the gatekeeper, "I am going" to close the gate.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the first option, because the speech is broken by 'said the gatekeeper', so both spoken parts take their own quotation marks.

mcqs.q: In the story 'Frogs', what was the competition?
options: A running competition to reach the top of a very high tower
A swimming race in a pond
A jumping competition in a field
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a running competition to the top of a very high tower, because the story begins with this goal.

mcqs.q: Why did one tiny frog succeed in reaching the top?
options: Because the crowd helped it climb
Because it took a rest halfway
Because the winner was deaf and could not hear the negative shouts
Because it was the biggest frog
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the winner was deaf, because the story says it turned out that the winner was deaf, so the negative words never reached it.

mcqs.q: What is the wisdom of the story 'Frogs'?
options: Never listen to other people when they are being negative or pessimistic, because they take away your most wonderful dreams
Never take part in any competition
Words have no power over our actions
mcqs.why: The correct answer is never to listen to negative or pessimistic people, because the story ends with this wisdom and the advice to say, 'With God's help I can do this.'

lessons.title: Writing: Summarizing a Poem and Writing an Application
lessons.notes_html:
How to Write: Summarizing a Poem

A summary of a poem is the story of the poem written in your own words. Follow the steps given in the book:

  • Find out the meanings of unfamiliar words.
  • Look at the title of the poem to see what it is about.
  • Read each stanza slowly, at least a couple of times, and try to understand what it means.
  • Read the poem as a whole to get the main idea.
  • Now start writing the story. Begin by giving the title of the poem and the name of the poet.
  • After this, write the key message of the poem. Finally, write down the story in your own words. You can use dialogues in direct speech.
  • Exchange your paper with another pair, give critical feedback, then edit for spelling, grammar and punctuation and rewrite the corrected story.

Summary: 'The Miller of the Dee' by Charles Mackay

Key message: Contentment and honest work bring more happiness than riches and power. A happy miller lived beside the river Dee. He worked and sang from morning to night, and his song was that he envied nobody and nobody envied him. Old King Hal said he was wrong: the king himself was sad though he was the king, and wished his heart were as light as the miller's. The miller smiled and said he earned his bread, loved his wife, his friend and his three children, owed no penny he could not pay, and thanked the river Dee that turned his mill to grind the corn to feed his children and himself. King Hal sighed and said the miller's cap was worth his crown and his mill worth his kingdom; such men are England's boast.

How to Write: Writing an Application

  • Begin your application with the person's name and organization.
  • Use formal language, brief informative sentences and short paragraphs.
  • Check your spelling, grammar and punctuation carefully. Follow the given format.
Part of the applicationWhat it contains
Date; name of recipient; designation; name of institution; name of cityThe heading of the application
SubjectThe relevant subject of the application
Dear Sir/Madam,The formal greeting
First paragraphHow you came to know about the job position and why you want to apply for it
Second paragraphWho you are, what you have done, and why you think you are suitable for this position
Third paragraphAsk for due consideration of the application and request for a positive reply
Thanking You. Yours sincerely,The closing, followed by the name and address of the sender

Remember: Model Applications

The model application for a teacher is addressed to The Principal, City Public School, Karachi, with the subject 'Application for the post of a teacher'. The applicant has passed M.A. in English and B.Ed. and has three years of teaching experience. The three vacant positions in Exercise 2 are: Subject teacher, Laboratory Assistant and Secretary; after writing, partners exchange applications and give each other positive feedback.

mcqs.q: What is the first step in summarizing a poem?
options: Find out the meanings of unfamiliar words
Write the key message at once
Exchange the paper with another pair
Give the title and the poet's name
mcqs.why: The correct answer is finding the meanings of unfamiliar words, because the book lists this as the first step before reading the stanzas closely.

mcqs.q: How should each stanza be read while preparing a summary?
options: Slowly, at least a couple of times, to understand what it means
Only the first line should be read
mcqs.why: The correct answer is slowly, at least a couple of times, because the book gives this step for understanding each stanza.

mcqs.q: With what should the written summary of a poem begin?
options: With a dialogue in direct speech
With the title of the poem and the name of the poet
With the key message of the poem
With critical feedback from another pair
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the title of the poem and the name of the poet, because the book says to begin the summary in this way.

mcqs.q: What is written after the title and the poet's name in a poem summary?
options: The key message of the poem
The story in the poet's exact words
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the key message of the poem, because the book's order is: title and poet, then the key message, then the story in your own words.

mcqs.q: What is the key message of 'The Miller of the Dee'?
options: A king is always happier than a worker
Contentment and honest work bring more happiness than riches and power
Money is the only source of happiness
Singing loudly makes a man rich
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that contentment and honest work bring more happiness than riches and power, because the happy miller is content while the rich king is sad.

mcqs.q: Why was the miller happy, according to his own answer?
options: Because he owned the whole river Dee
Because he earned his bread, loved his wife, friend and three children, and owed no penny he could not pay
Because he never worked at all
Because the king gave him a crown
mcqs.why: The correct answer is his honest earning, loved family and freedom from unpaid debt, because the miller lists exactly these reasons to King Hal.

mcqs.q: What did King Hal say at the end of the poem?
options: That the miller should stop singing
That the miller's song was wrong
That the river Dee belonged to the king
That the miller's cap was worth his crown and his mill worth his kingdom
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the miller's cap was worth the king's crown, because King Hal ends by calling such men England's boast.

mcqs.q: What does the first paragraph of a job application contain?
options: A request for a positive reply only
How you came to know about the job position and why you want to apply for it
The name and address of the sender
mcqs.why: The correct answer is how you came to know about the job and why you want to apply, because the book's format gives this content for the first paragraph.

mcqs.q: What does the second paragraph of a job application contain?
options: Who you are, what you have done, and why you think you are suitable for the position
mcqs.why: The correct answer is who you are, what you have done and why you are suitable, because the book's format gives this content for the second paragraph.

mcqs.q: How does a job application end?
options: With 'Thanking You. Yours sincerely,' followed by the name and address of the sender
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'Thanking You. Yours sincerely,' with the sender's name and address, because that is the closing given in the book's format.

lessons.title: Study Skills: Preparing, Giving and Evaluating Presentations
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 8.5 (Study Skills) teaches how to create and deliver simple presentations on various themes, problems and issues. This section is for acquiring additional language skills and is not to be formally assessed.

Key Points: Steps to Follow

  • Brainstorm.
  • Identify theme and focus.
  • Structure ideas and arguments in a coherent, logical fashion.
  • Support a subject or topic with effective factual information.
  • Develop and use cue cards.
  • Deliver the presentation.

How to Write and Practise

Students work in groups of three and prepare a presentation on the topic assigned by the teacher. The groups are numbered 1 to 5, and each number prepares its own topic. They get 10 minutes to prepare, decide who is going to deliver which part, and practise giving the presentation as a group before giving it in front of the class.

No.Presentation topic
1The importance of female education
2Drive Safety
3Punctuality in work and studies
4Cleanliness: self and surroundings
5The role that citizens can play in building a good society

Key Points: Evaluating a Presentation

The rest of the class listens carefully and evaluates each group on five items: topic and points clearly stated; organization of ideas; supporting details; body language (use of facial expressions and gestures); and eye contact. Each item is rated Exceptional (very good), Admirable (good), Acceptable (average) or Attempted (needed improvement), and students show their opinion by raising their hands.

Remember: Model Presentation

On 'The importance of female education': Speaker 1 (Introduction) says female education means giving girls the same chance to learn as boys, and it is the key to a better family and a better country. Speaker 2 (Points) says an educated girl becomes a good mother, a good teacher and a good citizen; she can earn, help her family and guide her children. Speaker 3 (Conclusion) says we should all send our girls to school and support them.

mcqs.q: What is the first step in preparing a presentation?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is brainstorm, because the book lists brainstorming as the first step before identifying the theme and focus.

mcqs.q: What comes after brainstorming in the presentation steps?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is identifying the theme and focus, because it is the second step in the book's list.

mcqs.q: How should ideas and arguments be structured in a presentation?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is in a coherent, logical fashion, because the book uses exactly these words for structuring ideas and arguments.

mcqs.q: With what should a subject or topic be supported in a presentation?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is effective factual information, because the book says to support a subject or topic in this way.

mcqs.q: What should presenters develop and use while delivering?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is cue cards, because 'develop and use cue cards' is one of the steps listed in the book.

mcqs.q: In the exercise, how do students prepare the presentation?
options: In groups of three, deciding who will deliver which part and practising as a group first
In groups of ten, reading from the book
By writing it at home only
mcqs.why: The correct answer is groups of three with divided parts and group practice, because the exercise gives exactly this method.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an evaluation item for presentations?
options: The colour of the classroom walls
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'topic and points clearly stated', because it is the first item in the book's evaluation table.

mcqs.q: What does the rating 'Attempted' mean in the evaluation?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'needed improvement', because the teacher's note explains Attempted as the rating for work that needed improvement.

mcqs.q: Which pair of things is judged under 'body language'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is facial expressions and gestures, because the evaluation table explains body language with these words in brackets.

mcqs.q: According to the model presentation, what does female education mean?
options: Giving girls the same chance to learn as boys
mcqs.why: The correct answer is giving girls the same chance to learn as boys, because Speaker 1 gives this meaning in the introduction of the model presentation.

lessons.title: Fun: Acting Out a Poem
lessons.notes_html:
About the Text

Unit 8.6 (Fun) is for having fun with language and is not to be formally assessed. Students act out the poem 'The Daffodils' by William Wordsworth in the form of a tableau. A tableau is a kind of performance where the actors act out a scene without using words. One student reads out (recites) the stanza while the others act it out, and the group that gives the best performance will be the winner.

How to Write and Perform: The Steps

  • Work in groups of five; each group is allotted one stanza of the poem. Groups calling out 1, 2, 3 and 4 do stanzas 1, 2, 3 and 4.
  • Step 1: Read the whole poem individually and then discuss how best you can act out the stanza allotted to your group.
  • Step 2: Select one person from your group who will recite the stanza while the other four act it out.
  • Step 3: Decide who will do what and quickly rehearse it. The book gives 10 minutes to prepare the tableau.

Summary: 'The Daffodils' by William Wordsworth

The poet wandered lonely as a cloud that floats high over valleys and hills, when all at once he saw a crowd, a host of golden daffodils beside the lake, beneath the trees, fluttering and dancing in the breeze. Continuous as the stars that shine and twinkle on the Milky Way, they stretched in a never-ending line along the margin of the bay; ten thousand he saw at a glance, tossing their heads in sprightly dance. The waves beside them danced, but the daffodils outdid the sparkling waves in glee, and a poet could not but be gay in such jocund (cheerful) company. Later, when he lies on his couch in vacant or in pensive mood, the daffodils flash upon that inward eye, which is the bliss of solitude, and then his heart with pleasure fills and dances with the daffodils.

Vocabulary

Word or lineMeaning in the poem
a host of golden daffodilsA large crowd of yellow daffodil flowers
sprightly danceA lively dance of the tossing flower heads
gleeJoy; the daffodils showed more joy than the waves
jocund companyCheerful company of the flowers
inward eyeThe mind's eye that sees the remembered scene
bliss of solitudeThe happiness of being alone with the memory

Remember

The memory of the daffodils is the poem's 'wealth': the poet little thought, while gazing, what wealth the show had brought him, but the scene returns later and fills his heart with pleasure.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the poem 'The Daffodils'?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is William Wordsworth, because the poem in Unit 8.6 is printed with his name under the title.

mcqs.q: What is a tableau?
options: A kind of performance where the actors act out a scene without using words
A card used by a presenter
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a performance where actors act out a scene without using words, because the teacher's note defines a tableau in exactly this way.

mcqs.q: How is the acting work divided in a group of five?
options: Two students recite and three act
One student recites the stanza while the other four act it out
The teacher recites for every group
mcqs.why: The correct answer is one reciter and four actors, because the steps say to select one person to recite while the other four act it out.

mcqs.q: What is the first step for acting out the poem?
options: Read the whole poem individually and then discuss how best to act out the allotted stanza
mcqs.why: The correct answer is reading the whole poem individually and discussing the acting, because it is Step 1 in the book's list.

mcqs.q: In the poem, the poet compares himself to what?
options: A star on the Milky Way
A lonely cloud floating high over valleys and hills
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a lonely cloud, because the poem opens with the line 'I wandered lonely as a cloud that floats on high o'er vales and hills'.

mcqs.q: Where were the daffodils, and what were they doing?
options: Beside the lake, beneath the trees, fluttering and dancing in the breeze
Inside the poet's house, in a vase
mcqs.why: The correct answer is beside the lake, beneath the trees, fluttering and dancing in the breeze, because these are the poem's own words in the first stanza.

mcqs.q: How many daffodils did the poet see at a glance?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ten thousand, because the second stanza says 'Ten thousand saw I at a glance, tossing their heads in sprightly dance'.

mcqs.q: What did the daffodils outdo in glee?
options: The stars of the Milky Way
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the sparkling waves, because the third stanza says the daffodils 'outdid the sparkling waves in glee'.

mcqs.q: What does the poet call 'the bliss of solitude'?
options: The inward eye on which the daffodils flash
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the inward eye, because the poem says the daffodils 'flash upon that inward eye, which is the bliss of solitude'.

mcqs.q: How does the poem end?
options: The poet sells the flowers in the market
The poet forgets the flowers forever
The poet plants daffodils at home
His heart with pleasure fills, and dances with the daffodils
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that his heart fills with pleasure and dances with the daffodils, because these are the last two lines of the poem.

lessons.title: Reading: The Healthy Living
lessons.notes_html:
Summary

Karim's grandparents were reaching the age of 80 but hardly looked a day older than 60. Every Sunday and on public holidays the family gathered at their house: 20 people in all, including Karim's father, two uncles, their wives, his aunty and uncle, and 10 cousins. One Sunday, Karim's younger cousin Zainab, who was studying in Grade 2, became excited by a soap advertisement on TV showing germs as monsters being fought by the soap. Karim laughed and said the ad was 'not real' and only made to sell products. Zainab spoke up: people had come to her school and told them how hand washing is extremely necessary to protect us, and her teacher had shown them how to wash hands properly and the critical times when we must wash both our hands.

Key Points

  • Hand washing prevents the direct transferring of germs into the mouth, the germs that cause diarrhea.
  • Karim argued that there was no soap when Dada was young, yet Dada stayed healthy. Zainab answered that other natural products were used when soap was not invented or widely available: Phitkari (Alum), Haldi (Turmeric), Neem leaves and Camphor; all these organic products are antiseptic and anti-bacterial.
  • Dada agreed with Zainab and her teacher. Diarrhea is one of the main causes of death among young children across the world, and only 12% of households in Pakistan use treated water.
  • Little acts of care bring a big change: drinking boiled water, keeping hands clean and germ free, and making communities aware of the harms of open defecation.
  • Karim also resolved to learn more about WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene) and to make his environment safe for children.

Key Points: When Should You Wash Your Hands?

Wash your handsWash your hands
After using the bathroomBefore and after eating or cooking food
After changing diapers or cleaning after a childBefore and after tending to someone who is sick
After coughing or sneezingBefore and after treating a cut or wound
After petting animals or touching meat or poultryAfter handling garbage or animal waste
After touching moneyAfter using the latrine (in Zainab's words)

Vocabulary and Language

Adjectives from the text include young, old, large, healthy, critical, harmful and natural; adverbs include extremely, properly, quietly and eagerly. Water in an area comes from tap water (water supply), hand pumps, wells and water tankers. It gets contaminated by open drains and garbage near the source, animal waste, open defecation and leaking pipes. Common ways of purifying water are boiling it, filtering it through a clean cloth or filter, using alum (Phitkari), and chlorination.

mcqs.q: How old were Karim's grandparents, and how old did they look?
options: They were reaching 80 but hardly looked a day older than 60
mcqs.why: The correct answer is reaching 80 but looking no older than 60, because the text opens with these ages for the grandparents.

mcqs.q: When did Karim's family gather at his grandparents' house?
options: Every Sunday and on public holidays
mcqs.why: The correct answer is every Sunday and on public holidays, because the text calls this gathering a family ritual on those days.

mcqs.q: What did Zainab's teacher show her class?
options: How to fight germs in an advertisement
How to wash hands properly and the critical times when we must wash both our hands
How to make soap at school
mcqs.why: The correct answer is how to wash hands properly and the critical times, because Zainab reports her teacher's lesson in these words.

mcqs.q: How does hand washing protect us, according to Zainab?
options: It makes the hands smell sweet
It kills all pollution in the air
It replaces the need for clean water
It prevents the direct transferring of germs into the mouth, the germs that cause diarrhea
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it prevents germs reaching the mouth, because Zainab gives this reason for hand washing in the text.

mcqs.q: Which natural products were used before soap, according to Zainab?
options: Phitkari (Alum), Haldi (Turmeric), Neem leaves and Camphor
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Phitkari, Haldi, Neem leaves and Camphor, because Zainab lists these organic products, which are antiseptic and anti-bacterial.

mcqs.q: What did Dada say about diarrhea?
options: It is cured by soap advertisements
It is one of the main causes of death among young children across the world
It is a very rare disease
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that diarrhea is one of the main causes of death among young children, because Dada states this fact in the text.

mcqs.q: What percentage of households in Pakistan use treated water, according to Dada?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is only 12%, because Dada says 'Only 12% households in Pakistan use treated water.'

mcqs.q: Which of these is a time when you should wash your hands, from the book's list?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is after coughing or sneezing, because the book's list 'When should you wash your hands' includes this time.

mcqs.q: Which is a common way of purifying water given in the lesson work?
options: Storing it in an open bucket
Keeping it in the sun all day
mcqs.why: The correct answer is boiling the water, because the collected information lists boiling, filtering, using alum (Phitkari) and chlorination as purifying methods.

mcqs.q: What is one of the declamation contest topics of this lesson?
options: 'A hand washed is a life saved'
'You get respect if you give respect'
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 'A hand washed is a life saved', because it is the first declamation topic listed in Task 2 of The Healthy Living.

lessons.title: Reading: You Are What You Eat
lessons.notes_html:
Summary

Abeera lived in a village in Shikarpur. She was eagerly waiting for the winter vacations because her family would attend her aunt's wedding in Karachi, the biggest city of Sindh, famous for its lights, cityscapes and sea, in the last week of December. Her class teacher, Ms. Seema, asked her to share her travel experience with the whole class when she returned. In Karachi, almost every day Abeera ate food cooked outside, oily, spicy and fried food, and she began to feel very sick and nauseous. She was yearning to go back home, sleep properly and eat home-cooked food. Back at school she complained that she could not fully enjoy the experience because of her health.

Key Points

  • Zain said it must be the oil and spice; Aisha said she ate food which was not home cooked; Raheem said her stomach got tired because she ate more food than her normal diet.
  • Ms. Seema explained that the human body needs not only a balanced diet but also a proper routine to function; anything that disturbs the routine takes a toll on the body and mind.
  • A balanced diet is a good combination of proteins, carbohydrates and fats, consumed through healthy food sources. The food groups are vegetables and fruits, dairy, fibre, and meat and poultry; vegetables and fruits should be consumed more frequently than meat or mutton.
  • Home-cooked food is not automatically balanced: a diet without balance results in food deficiency and malnutrition.
  • Young children (0-3 years) are most affected. Malnourishment in the early stages of childhood can lead to irreversible damage to physical growth, called stunting: low height for age.
